title: Smoked Indian Naan
description: Buttery, crisp, and cozy, this Indian flatbread is infused with a smoky flavor, perfect for any meal. It's also dairy-free friendly and can be made in under an hour.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a flaky sea salt for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional, but adds a touch of sweetness.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Use a thermometer to check the temperature.

ingredients.name: Whole wheat flour
ingredients.notes: You can also use all-purpose flour, but whole wheat gives a nuttier flavor.

ingredients.name: Smoked olive oil
ingredients.notes: Use a high-quality, extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Fresh cilantro
ingredients.notes: Chopped or torn, whichever you prefer.

ingredients.name: Garlic powder
ingredients.notes: Optional, but adds depth to the naan.

ingredients.name: Chopped scallions
ingredients.notes: Optional, but adds a nice crunch.

ingredients.name: Poppy seeds
ingredients.notes: Optional, but adds a nutty flavor.

instructions: Combine yeast, salt, sugar, and warm water in a large mixing bowl. Let it sit for 5-7 minutes, or until the yeast is activated and frothy.
Add flour, smoked olive oil, cilantro, lemon juice, garlic powder, black pepper, and scallions to the bowl. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
Divide the dough into 4-6 equal pieces, depending on how large you want your naan to be. Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten it slightly into an oval shape.
Place the naan on the preheated skillet or griddle and cook for 1-2 minutes, or until it starts to bubble and the edges start to curl.
Flip the naan over and cook for another 1-2 minutes, or until it is golden brown and crispy.
Brush the naan with melted butter or ghee, if desired.
Repeat with the remaining dough pieces, until all the naan are cooked.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro and lemon wedges, if desired.
